body:
## Problem

With `jumpoptions+=view`, jump-list entries save the relative topline and horizontal skip, but not filler lines above the topline. Virtual or diff filler above the first displayed buffer line is therefore lost after jumping away and back.

A saved filler count can also become stale before the jump returns. Restoring it without validation can produce an impossible view and cause later viewport correction to discard the saved topline.

## Solution

Store `w_topfill` in `fmarkv_T` with the topline offset and skip column.

Before restoring, copy the saved mark view because fold and diff queries may evaluate user code. Clamp the computed topline to the current buffer, query filler only for a positive saved value, and verify that the target window and buffer still exist after that query. Restore only currently available filler and use `check_topfill(..., false)` so a short window reduces the filler count without moving the restored topline.

When checking whether filler fits, account for wrapped rows already hidden by `smoothscroll` and `skipcol`. The actual-filler clamp remains at the mark restoration boundary; applying it to every `check_topfill()` caller breaks valid EOF diff-filler scrolling state.

This PR intentionally does not change `winrestview()`; validation of arbitrary dictionaries and its existing `down=true` behavior are separate concerns.

## Testing

The jump tests use attached screens and cover:

- virtual lines that remain present;
- virtual lines removed before restoration;
- a shorter window that must reduce filler without moving topline;
- diff filler that disappears before the return jump;
- a wrapped topline where `smoothscroll` hides rows through `skipcol`.

```sh
make functionaltest TEST_FILE=test/functional/editor/jump_spec.lua
```

The complete jump suite, related move/normal/scrollbind tests, the EOF diff-filler oldtest, lint, and documentation checks pass locally.

## AI disclosure

AI tools assisted with the analysis, implementation, and tests. The commit includes the generic `AI-assisted` token.

comment_regular_data.body: somewhat related: would also be wonderful to have better viewport restoration after exiting diff-mode
That would be useful too. I may look into viewport restoration after leaving diff mode in a separate PR later, keeping this one focused on restoring filler lines in saved jump views.

AI findings:


<details>
<summary>AI findings details</summary>

>  **`w_topfill` is restored without validating it against the filler lines that actually exist** (mark.c:702) — unlike the neighbouring `skipcol` restore. `check_topfill()` only bounds against window height, so a stale value survives.
>
>  Repro: `:set jumpoptions=view`; an extmark supplies 3 `virt_lines` above line 10; scroll to `topline=10, topfill=3`; `G` captures it; then delete the extmark (or `:e!`, or `zf` a closed fold over line 10). `<C-o>` sets `w_topfill = 3` 
>  while `win_get_fill(curwin, 10) == 0`. The next `update_topline()` trips `wp->w_topfill > win_get_fill(...)` (move.c:342) → `scroll_cursor_top()` (move.c:1888-1893) overwrites topline/topfill and calls `reset_skipcol()`. **Both the 
>  restored topline and the restored skipcol are discarded — the view restore ends up worse than before the patch.** Separately, `get_rel_pos()` (buffer.c:3572) computes `above = 9 + 0 - 3 = 6`, so the ruler percentage is wrong (larger 
>  fills print "Top").
>
>  Fix: `curwin->w_topfill = MIN(fm->view.topfill, win_get_fill(curwin, curwin->w_topline));`
>
>  **`check_topfill(curwin, true)` may scroll the topline away** (mark.c:703). Saved `topline=10, topfill=4` in a 6-row window, later resized to 3 rows: the `down && wp->w_topline > 1` branch does `w_topline--; w_topfill = 0`
>  (move.c:1665-1667). You get line 9 with no fill — neither the saved topline nor the saved fill, and `w_botline` is left one off. Every other "clamp the fill, keep the line" caller passes `false` (mouse.c:1518, 1548; diff.c:741).
>
>  **The `w_skipcol` guard then uses a stale local `topline`** (mark.c:705) — `check_topfill()` may have just decremented `curwin->w_topline`, but the guard still evaluates `hasFolding()` and `linetabsize_eol()` against the old value. With 
>  `'smoothscroll'` a saved skipcol gets accepted for a line it was never measured against: exactly the two conditions the guard exists to reject. Use `curwin->w_topline`.
>
>  **Altitude:** the clamp belongs inside `check_topfill()` (move.c:1659). Its docstring says "Don't end up with too many filler lines in the window" but it never bounds by `win_get_fill()`; every caller that raises `w_topfill` pre-clamps 
>  by convention (mouse.c:1501, 1511, 1545; move.c:1381, 1888). The two places restoring an *external* value — `f_winrestview()` (eval/window.c:856) and now `mark_view_restore()` — both skip it and both inherit the bug. One line at the top 
>  of `check_topfill()` fixes both and removes the need for a special case.
>
>  ### Tests
>
>  - jump_spec.lua:399 asserts only `winsaveview().topfill` with no screen attached, while every sibling in `describe('jumpoptions=view')` uses `Screen.new(12, 8)` + `screen:expect()`. It would pass with a wrong topline, an undrawn virt 
>  line, or a post-restore scroll — i.e. all three findings above. It also runs 80x24 against a 30-line file, so `check_topfill()`'s clamping branch (the only new call the patch adds) never executes.
>  - No case where the saved topfill is *invalid* at restore time — the extmark stays alive across the round trip, so the unclamped assignment is indistinguishable from a clamped one.
>  - Convention: this duplicates `it('restores the view')` at jump_spec.lua:382 (same `edit`, same `G`/`<C-o>`), differing only by the extmark and which field it reads — the assertions belong there.
>

</details>

Thanks, these findings are valid. I updated the commit in [`d1ca1b9611`](https://github.com/wrvsrx/neovim/commit/d1ca1b96119605505b391d47c206a304288490b1).

- `check_topfill()` now clamps `w_topfill` against `win_get_fill(wp, wp->w_topline)`, so the invariant is enforced for both jump restoration and `winrestview()` instead of only at this call site.
- `mark_view_restore()` calls `check_topfill(curwin, false)`, which clamps the restored fill without moving the restored topline when the window is shorter.
- The `skipcol` guard now checks `curwin->w_topline`, avoiding the stale local value.

The jump test now uses an attached `Screen` and verifies the rendered view while the virtual lines still exist, after the extmark has been removed before restoration, and in a short window where the saved fill must be clamped without changing the topline. It also covers stale `topfill` passed through `winrestview()`.

I kept the existing `check_topfill(wp, true)` call in `f_winrestview()`: the common actual-filler clamp fixes its stale-value case, while preserving its existing behavior when valid filler exceeds the window height.

The jump, move, normal, API window, and scrollbind test suites pass, as do the build and lint targets.

Follow-up: the first revision put the actual-filler clamp in `check_topfill()`, but the full CI oldtests showed that this was too broad. Internal scrolling legitimately uses `w_topfill` during EOF diff filler handling with `scrolloffpad`; clamping every `check_topfill()` call changed that behavior on all oldtest platforms.

I revised the fix in [`7b28cfac3f`](https://github.com/wrvsrx/neovim/commit/7b28cfac3f): `check_topfill()` retains its existing internal semantics, while saved `topfill` is clamped specifically at the two external restoration boundaries, `mark_view_restore()` and `winrestview()`. `mark_view_restore()` still uses `check_topfill(curwin, false)`, and the `skipcol` checks still use the resulting `curwin->w_topline`.

`Test_scrolloffpad_diff_eof_filler_behavior()` now passes locally together with the 19 jump tests and 144 API window tests. This keeps the stale-value fix without changing unrelated scrolling state.

<details>
<summary>AI findings</summary>


**Negative `topfill` escapes the clamp** (eval/window.c:881). `MIN(-3, win_get_fill(...))` keeps `-3`, and `check_topfill()` can't rescue it:

```c
void check_topfill(win_T *wp, bool down)
{
  if (wp->w_topfill > 0) {     // ← negative falls straight through
```

`:call winrestview({'lnum':3,'topline':3,'topfill':-3})` then survives `:redraw!` and nvim emits `grid_cursor_goto [grid=1, row=-3, col=0]` — out-of-grid for real UIs, and it trips the test-UI assertion at screen.lua:1113. Needs clamping
into `[0, win_get_fill(...)]`, not `MIN`.

**`win_get_fill()` on every mark-view restore can run arbitrary Vimscript** (mark.c:702). It's now called unconditionally, even when `fm->view.topfill == 0`: `win_get_fill` → `diff_check_fill` → `diff_check_with_linestatus`, whose first
act is `if (curtab->tp_diff_invalid) { ex_diffupdate(NULL); }`. With `'jumpoptions'` containing `view` in a diff tabpage, every `<C-o>` triggers a full diff refresh — with `'diffexpr'` set, that's user script. If it wipes a buffer or
closes the window, `w_jumplist[]`/`tagstack[]` is reallocated and the reads of `fm->view.skipcol`/`fm->view.topfill` two lines later are use-after-free. Guard on `fm->view.topfill > 0`.

**Out-of-range topline is now measured** (mark.c:701). `buflist_getfpos()` clamps `w_cursor.lnum`, not `fm->mark.lnum`, so a shrunk buffer gives `topline = ml_line_count + 1`. `diff_check_with_linestatus` accepts that (it only rejects `>
ml_line_count + 1`) and returns end-of-buffer fill, so `check_topfill` calls `plines_win_nofill(wp, ml_line_count + 1, true)` → `ml_get_buf` on an invalid lnum. Previously `w_topfill` was always 0 here, so the line was never measured.

**The two restore paths disagree on `down`** (eval/window.c:883). `mark_view_restore` passes `false` (keep the topline), `winrestview()` still passes `true` (discard it). `winrestview({'lnum':11,'topline':10,'topfill':4})` in a 2-row
window ends at topfill 0, while the PR's own test asserts `{10, 1}` for the equivalent mark-path state. The commit message claims "keep the restored topline when the window is too short" but implements half of it, so identical inputs now
yield different views.

**Ordering vs skipcol** (mark.c:703) — `check_topfill()` runs before `w_skipcol` is restored and doesn't account for it: topline wrapping 5 rows with skipcol hiding 4 and `topfill = 3` in a 6-row window gives `n = 5`, so topfill drops to
1 even though 3 would fit.

## Structure

The altitude point from the last round still stands, and is now stronger: `check_topfill()` is *named* "don't end up with too many filler lines" yet never bounds by `win_get_fill()`. Folding `wp->w_topfill = MIN(wp->w_topfill,
win_get_fill(wp, wp->w_topline));` in at the top fixes ~10 existing callers plus both new sites, and lets both special cases **and** `topfill_set` be deleted.

`topfill_set` (eval/window.c:840, 860, 880) is a parallel flag for a derivable condition — your "Calculate, don't track" rule. The clamp is a no-op when `topfill` was absent (`set_topline()` already zeroed `w_topfill`), so running it
unconditionally removes the flag and both assignments with no behavior change.

The skipcol guard change (mark.c:705, `topline` → `curwin->w_topline`) is a no-op sold as a fix in the commit message: `set_topline()` differs only by fold-start snapping, and `hasFolding()` returns true for both a line inside a closed
fold and its start line, so the guard short-circuits identically and `linetabsize_eol()` never sees a differing lnum.

## Tests & docs

- No diff-mode coverage at all — both tests use extmark `virt_lines`, but `win_get_fill()` is `decor_virt_lines() + diff_check_fill()`, and the diff half is where the `ex_diffupdate` re-entry, the end-of-buffer fill, and the closed-fold
zeroing live. A regression there ships green.
- jump_spec.lua:423-425 appends a pure `winrestview`/`winsaveview` assertion to `'restores the view'` — no jump involved. Belongs with the winrestview tests, and it's inconsistent that the fourth scenario got its own `it()`.
- motion.txt:832 still describes `mark-view` as just the topline offset (`skipcol` was already missing, `topfill` now too). And `winrestview()` silently discarding a caller's `topfill` is a divergence from Vim — Vim's `f_winrestview`
calls only `check_topfill()` — with nothing in vimfn.txt, vim_diff.txt, or news.txt.

</details>

Thanks, I revised the commit again (`6bf69c97e7`).

- The `winrestview()` change and its `topfill_set` flag are removed from this PR. Negative arbitrary dictionary values and `winrestview()`'s existing `down=true` behavior are separate from jump-mark storage.
- `mark_view_restore()` now copies all saved mark/view fields before fold or diff queries, clamps the computed topline before measuring it, queries filler only when the saved topfill is positive, and verifies the target window and buffer after the query.
- The `skipcol` ordering is fixed: it is validated before the topfill fit check, and `check_topfill()` now subtracts wrapped rows already hidden by smooth scrolling.
- I kept the actual-filler clamp at the external mark-restoration boundary. Applying it unconditionally inside `check_topfill()` caused `Test_scrolloffpad_diff_eof_filler_behavior()` to fail on all oldtest platforms because internal EOF diff scrolling has valid transient topfill state not represented by `win_get_fill()` at the current topline.
The pure `winrestview()` assertion was removed from the jump test. Added Screen-backed coverage now includes disappearing diff filler and combined topfill/skipcol restoration, and `motion.txt` documents all saved mark-view fields.

The complete 21-test jump suite, related move/normal/scrollbind tests, the EOF diff-filler oldtest, lint, and documentation checks pass locally.
